pages.text: Beyond the core leveling system, Penchant's features are organized into $(#7A2FBF)modules$(), each shipped as a built-in datapack you can enable or disable independently.

$(bold)Configuring modules$()$(br)Toggle them in the $(#7A2FBF)Data Packs$() screen when creating a world, or later with the $(#7A2FBF)/datapack$() command. A menu mod such as Datapack/Gamerule Menus also works.$(br2)This is the recommended way for players. Changing packs never rewrites an existing world's selection unless you do it yourself.

$(bold)Modpack defaults$()$(br)Pack developers can change which modules are pre-selected for $(italic)new$() worlds in $(#7A2FBF)config/penchant/server.toml$(). That file does $(bold)not$() affect worlds that already exist.$(br2)Some modules make more sense together; these soft recommendations are noted on each page.

pages.title: Data Packs
pages.text: Each Penchant module appears as its own datapack in the world creation screen.

$(italic)Enabled by default$()$(br)$(li)Table Rework $(li)Bookshelf Placement $(li)Durability Rework $(li)Loot Rework $(li)No Anvil Books $(li)Guaranteed Drops$(br2)Curse rarity is part of Loot Rework, not a separate pack. Randomized librarians are not available on this Minecraft version.
